rv.q: McKnight makes a better fist of it than most.
Tron Theatre Company has once again given us a festive treat that should not be kept for Christmas Day but should be unwrapped and visited as much as you can.
This panto is a non-traditional treat.
Johnny McKnight’s Gallus in Weegieland is a bold, brash and unapologetically Glaswegian romp which proves, without a doubt, that the Tron Theatre pantomime is a festive must-see.
Gallus In Weegieland roars to a merry conclusion, in a riot of wildly inventive design, outrageous one-liners and true Christmas spirit, fully reimagined for the age we live in.

cn.t: Critics praise this bold Glaswegian panto revival for its razor-sharp wit, topical references, and progressive approach to the genre. Louise McCarthy's athletic Queenie of Hearts stands out in McKnight's riotously entertaining reimagining of Alice in Wonderland.
